a wave of beer taller than a house smashed through London…
and killed eight people.
It started inside the Horse Shoe Brewery.
A giant wooden vat, twenty-two feet tall, held more than three thousand barrels of beer.
Huge iron hoops kept it together.
On October 17th,
one of those hoops snapped.
Nobody panicked.
An hour later, the whole vat exploded.
The blast smashed the vat beside it…
and then another.
Over a million litres of beer burst through the brewery wall.
A fifteen-foot wave tore into St Giles,
one of the poorest slums in London.
It crushed homes and flooded cellars where whole families lived.
In one basement,
mourners had gathered for a little boy's wake.
Five of them drowned.
Rescuers dug through the wreckage for hours.
So who paid for it?
Nobody.
A jury ruled it an accident.
And the brewery?
The government gave it back the tax it had paid on all the lost beer.
Eight people died…
and the brewery got a refund.
